instruction: Convert all currently open blog posts to PDFs and store them in /home/user/Documents/Blog with filenames matching their titles.

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating /home/user/Documents/Blog directory structure and saving 2 PDFs with filenames based on article titles. Evaluator checks four aspects with partial credit: (1) directory exists (25%), (2) is actually a directory not a file (25%), (3) contains at least 2 PDFs (25%), (4) PDF filenames contain keywords from article titles like 'agent', 'human', 'data', 'quality' (25%). Custom getter retrieves directory info and PDF filenames, metric provides progressive scoring.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.25 for directory exists, +0.25 for is_directory, +0.25 for >=2 PDFs, +0.25 for filenames containing article title keywords

llm_judge_reasons: COMPLETE COVERAGE: Evaluator now checks all 4 requirements from instruction: (1) directory exists, (2) is a directory, (3) contains >=2 PDFs, (4) PDF filenames contain article title keywords
CORRECT GETTER LOGIC: Getter successfully extracts directory info, PDF count, and actual PDF filenames using bash commands
SEMANTIC FILENAME VERIFICATION: Metric checks that at least 2 PDFs have filenames containing keywords from article titles ('agent', 'human', 'data', 'quality') which correspond to the blog post URLs
PROGRESSIVE SCORING: Partial credit logic (25% per requirement) makes semantic sense for multi-step task
KEYWORD-BASED APPROACH: Using keywords from article URLs is pragmatic and robust - handles title variations while ensuring PDFs relate to the blog posts
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor enhancement: Consider making keyword matching slightly stricter (e.g., require each PDF to match different keywords to ensure both blog posts are saved, not just 2 PDFs with 'agent' in the name)
